title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: CDC assistance schemes
sections.summary: Local Community Development Councils have schemes for short-term and long-term assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Local Community Development Councils (CDCs) have schemes in place for both short-term and long-term assistance.

sections.label: Minister update request
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Minister can give an update on these plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can Minister give an update on these plans?

sections.label: Marriage courses on ROM website
sections.summary: Marriage courses on the Registry of Marriage's website include some costing about $300, one titled "Evidence-based Marriage Programme".

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One useful way is to review the marriage courses available on the Registry of Marriage's website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I note that some of them cost about $300 and the titles include one called "Evidence-based Marriage Programme".

sections.label: Marriage course cost and subsidy
sections.summary: Courses cost a few hundred dollars with a $70 Government subsidy, and a question asks how to make them more accessible and affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some of these courses cost a few hundred dollars and I understand that the Government provides a subsidy of $70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How can the Government make these programmes more accessible and affordable to better support couples in building strong foundations for their families?

sections.label: Food insecurity among families
sections.summary: Nearly half of a sample of 236 families in Singapore reported moderate to severe food insecurity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet nearly half of a sample of 236 families in Singapore reported moderate to severe food insecurity.

sections.label: Minimum Income Standards food cost
sections.summary: The 2019 Minimum Income Standards study found a single elderly household needs about $400 a month for food, about 29% of their budget.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The 2019 Minimum Income Standards study led by Dr Ng Kok Hoe of the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy found that a single elderly household requires about $400 a month for food, about 29% of their budget.

sections.label: Food spending in low-income Chinese families
sections.summary: A study of 77 low-income Chinese families with young children found healthier diets cost $204 per person monthly versus $168.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: The purpose was to understand consumption of food in 77 low-income Chinese families with young children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: They found that families who ate a healthier diet – more fresh fruits, vegetables and meat, less processed food – spent significantly more each month than families who did not – $204 per capita, per month, instead of $168.

sections.label: US food stamps and grocery vouchers
sections.summary: US research found food stamps reduced food insecurity and improved health, so Budget 2020's grocery vouchers are a step forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: Research from the United States has found that government food stamps reduced food insecurity, increased birth weight, improved children’s health, and even reduced metabolic linked diseases such as obesity, high blood pressure and diabetes, many years down the road, for people who benefited from food stamps when they were children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: So, Budget 2020’s initiative to grant $100 in grocery vouchers, for two years, for needy Singaporeans is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: But much more can be done if addressing food insecurity is made a priority of government policy, rather than left to voluntary groups.

sections.label: Long-term programme for food insecure households
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry has a long-term programme to reduce food insecure households in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, above the $100 in grocery vouchers between FY 2020 and FY 2021, is the Ministry implementing any long-term programme to reduce the number of food insecure households in Singapore?

sections.label: Tracking lower income HDB residents
sections.summary: The question asks whether MSF tracks income, expenditures and financial well-being of lower income HDB residents after survey findings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, last year's Household Expenditure Survey revealed that between 2013 and 2018, Singaporeans living in 1-room and 2-room flats have increased their monthly spending by 3.7% on average, while families in private apartments saw expenditure fall by 0.1%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singstat also reported that households in the lowest 20% income group experienced an expenditure increase which was more than their income growth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Does MSF have a programme to track the income, expenditures and financial well-being of lower income HDB residents?

sections.label: Housing and utilities expenditure by flat type
sections.summary: Average household expenditure per member on Housing and Utilities is higher in 1-room and 2-room flats than 4-room and 5-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In absolute terms, the average household expenditure per household member on Housing and Utilities for those living in 1-room and 2-room flats is higher than those living in 4-room and 5-room flats.

sections.label: Singaporeans earning less than expenditure
sections.summary: A survey found at least 20% of Singaporeans earn less than their monthly expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: According to a survey, there are least 20% of Singaporeans who are earning less than their monthly expenditure.

sections.label: Pre-school placement for low-income children
sections.summary: A higher percentage of children from these families are not in pre-schools, and MSF is asked to ensure all are placed in pre-schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Four, a higher percentage of the children of these families is not in pre-schools when it is even more crucial for them to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can MSF ensure that all of these children are placed in pre-schools?

sections.label: Disadvantage and transnational families in need
sections.summary: Those from low-income single parent families face higher chance of disadvantage, and more transnational families belong to families in need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Six, there is higher chance of those from low-income single parent families of being disadvantaged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Seven, there are more transnational families who belong to the families in need.

sections.label: Rough sleepers in Singapore report
sections.summary: A November 2019 LKY School of Public Policy report revealed about 1,000 rough sleepers on Singapore streets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the LKY School of Public Policy report published in November 2019, it was revealed that there are about 1,000 rough sleepers on the streets of Singapore.

sections.label: Destitute Persons Act residency requirement
sections.summary: The Destitute Persons Act defines a destitute person as an idle person with no residence, so rough sleepers with a residence cannot be required to take shelter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As currently worded, a "destitute person" under the Destitute Persons Act is defined as, inter alia, "any idle person found in a public place, who has no place of residence".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Based on this definition, there is no ability to require a rough sleeper who has a residence to take shelter in welfare homes for the sake of his health and welfare under the Destitute Persons Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I believe there is a case to remove the residency requirement.

sections.label: Inclusivity of Break the Silence campaign
sections.summary: It is asked whether the next Break the Silence campaign could explicitly recognise LGBTQ+ persons and other marginalised groups.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: Could the next Break the Silence campaign be made more inclusive, by explicitly recognising the vulnerabilities of LGBTQ+ persons and other marginalised groups?

sections.label: Children and Young Persons Act protection
sections.summary: Children's rights are protected by the Children and Young Persons Act, and amendments extended identity protection to children aged 17 and 18.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the rights of children are protected by the Children and Young Persons Act.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad to have been in the House when we passed the amendments to extend identity protection for young people involved in court proceedings to children aged 17 and 18.

sections.label: Protecting children's digital rights
sections.summary: A speaker asks MSF to lead a whole-of-Government effort to protect children's digital rights, including privacy and data protection.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But there is much more we can do to expressly protect children's digital rights, especially in the areas of the privacy and data protection.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must take more active measures to ensure that their personal data is processed fairly, lawfully, accurately and securely, for specific purposes and with the free, explicit, informed and unambiguous consent of children and their parents.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given MSF's significant efforts in advancing the welfare of children, I would like to ask the Ministry to lead the charge in driving a whole-of- Government effort to recognise, concretise and protect the digital rights of children.

sections.label: Update on Act amendment initiatives
sections.summary: A question asks the Ministry to provide an update on new initiatives implemented since the Act's amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the new initiatives that have been implemented since the Act's amendment?

sections.label: Delta League 10th year
sections.summary: Delta League marks its 10th year, with over 20,000 youths benefiting from its programmes in the past nine years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Delta League marks its 10th year this year, with over 20,000 youths benefiting from its programmes in the past nine years.

sections.label: Singapore ratified UN disability convention
sections.summary: Singapore ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013.

sections.label: UN Convention Article 27 implementation
sections.summary: A question asks the Government's assessment of implementing the UN Convention's Article 27 on Work and Employment, citing employment schemes and rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has had schemes to boost the hiring of persons with disabilities, including the latest announcement of the Enabling Employment Credit, to provide stronger wage support for open employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a recent Parliamentary answer, MOM stated that the resident employment rate of persons with disabilities in the working age of 15 to 64 was about 29%, with the resident unemployment rate at 13%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is the Government’s assessment of how far Singapore has implemented the UN Convention, particularly Article 27 on Work and Employment?

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan progress update
sections.summary: A question asks for an update on the Enabling Masterplan's progress and the work of two workgroups on employment and independent living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am appreciative of the efforts that have been put in to provide support to families with children with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, what else can be done to bring greater convenience to PWDs and their care-givers in accessing social services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Two workgroups, for instance, were commissioned – one to look at employment and the other on independent living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans, especially PWDs and their families are not aware of the progress of the latest Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the progress of the Masterplan and what has so far been done by the two workgroups?

sections.label: Future planning for disabled children
sections.summary: The speaker urges MSF to assemble a team to improve future planning for families with disabled children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The question ought to be shifted to, “What is going to happen in the future when I am gone, and how can I shape it?” I urge MSF to assemble a team to improve the current state of future planning for families with disabled children.

sections.label: Housing and support choices for PWDs
sections.summary: The speaker urges MSF to develop a Singapore continuum of housing and support choices for PWDs based on family support, ability and service needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Yet, at the same time, taxation on personal income and corporate taxes are low, contributing to lower public spendings on social services, especially for PWDs compared to other countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I urge MSF to develop our uniquely Singapore continuum of housing and support choices for PWDs depending on: the level of family support and financial ability; the level of ability of the PWD himself in independent daily living and work; and the level of support services needed by them in care supervision, healthcare, daily living and work.

sections.label: EIPIC intervention hours shortfall
sections.summary: EIPIC offers up to 12 hours of intervention a week, less than half the 25 to 40 hours some experts postulated is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, the Government-subsidised Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) helps to pay for therapy and intervention programmes that typically offer up to 12 hours of intervention a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: But this is less than half of the lower bound of the range of between 25 to 40 hours a week, that some experts postulated is needed for effectiveness.

sections.label: Operators listed under scheme
sections.summary: Currently, only 10 operators are listed under the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, only 10 operators are listed under the scheme.

sections.label: Monthly fees of $832
sections.summary: The fees at $832 a month are not low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: The fees at $832 a month are not low.

sections.label: Subsidies by family income
sections.summary: Low-income families earning under $1,500 get 90% subsidy, while those earning over $3,500 get 10%, paying more than $700 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Subsidies are generous now for low-income families – those with income of less than $1,500, they get 90% subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: However, for those who earn more than $3,500, they get a subsidy of only 10% – leaving them to pay more than $700 each month.

sections.label: Mandatory parenting courses proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes MSF make parenting courses mandatory for new parents and link attendance to Baby Bonus entitlements, citing rising child abuse referrals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Parenting is a complex balancing act, which requires both making hard decisions between giving the child freedom to grow and being there for them when needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I noticed, with regret, that data from MSF showed a gradual rise in the number of children referred to MSF for various forms of abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, we should acknowledge that not all parents may be equipped with the right skillset and mindset to raise the child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to propose to MSF to consider making parenting courses mandatory for all new parents and incentivise parents to attend such courses by making it a prerequisite to receive their Baby Bonus entitlements.

sections.label: Triple P programme attendance rates
sections.summary: The speaker asks about attendance and success rates of MSF's nation-wide Triple P Positive Parenting Programme in schools.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: I can throw them out if you want me to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
sentences.text: I understand that MSF has implemented the Triple P Positive Parenting Programme nation-wide in schools and I would like to find out more about the attendance and success rates of these courses.

sections.label: Family justice reforms update request
sections.summary: The speaker asks for an update on the family justice committee's recommendations and key proposals, and the reply concerned shared care and control rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Last year, the Committee to review and enhance reforms in the family justice system submitted its recommendations to make various processes less acrimonious for families undergoing divorce, particularly for those with children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Could the Ministry provide an update on this matter and the specifics on the key proposals which should be adopted and implemented?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The reply was that parents with shared care and control arrangements have equal rights to list their child as an essential occupier and they should come to a mutually agreeable decision themselves.

sections.label: Shared care and HDB occupier listing
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MSF can require divorce rulings awarding shared care and control to state which party may list the child as an essential occupier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the welfare of the child, can MSF require divorce rulings that award shared care and control to also state which party is allowed to list the child as an essential occupier in their application to buy a subsidised HDB flat?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With a median salary of only $600 a month, single unwed parents under 35 years old clearly need the cash.

sections.label: Baby Bonus for single unwed parents
sections.summary: The speaker calls for ending discrimination by giving single unwed parents a cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us end the discrimination and provide single unwed parents with a cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sections.label: Mothers taking break after childbirth
sections.summary: Surveys show that 72% of mothers in Singapore take some form of break after childbirth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Surveys have shown that 72% of mothers here take some form of break after childbirth.

sections.label: Foreign teacher outbreak impact
sections.summary: Asks how many foreign teachers were affected by the outbreak and whether MSF will adjust foreign-local pre-school teacher ratios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How many of these foreign teachers have been affected by the outbreak?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Using this outbreak as a learning point, will MSF consider adjusting the ratio of foreign and the local pre-school teachers to prevent the recurrence of a similar situation where there is a sudden drop in teaching staff?

sections.label: Attracting locals to pre-school
sections.summary: Asks whether MSF has new plans to attract more Singaporeans and mid-career individuals into pre-school education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Does MSF have new plans to attract more Singaporeans and mid-career individuals to join the pre-school education sector?

sections.label: School-based student care fees
sections.summary: Asks how fees across all school-based Student Care Centres can be kept fair as capacity is ramped up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): Dual-income families are becoming the norm and, naturally, demand for more full-day pre-school and after-school student care services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was announced in last year's Committee of Supply that all Primary schools would have after-school care facilities within the school compound by the end of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we ramp up capacity to meet demand, how do we ensure that fees across all school-based Student Care Centres (SCCs) are fair?

sections.label: Government-supported pre-school places
sections.summary: States that at the 2019 National Day Rally, PM Lee announced more Government-supported pre-school places, including extending the Partner Operator Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the National Day Rally in 2019, Prime Minister Lee announced that the Government would be increasing Government-supported pre-school places to improve accessibility to affordable and quality pre-schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Measures to be adopted include the extension of the Partner Operator (POP) Scheme, which will improve the affordability, accessibility and quality of POP services through Government funding and support.

sections.label: Means-tested subsidy income ceiling
sections.summary: States that part of the spending increase raises the household monthly income ceiling from $7,500 to $12,000, helping about 30,000 more families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Part of this increase in spending is to raise the number of families that are eligible for additional means-tested subsidies by raising the household monthly income ceiling from $7,500 to $12,000, thereby helping an additional 30,000-odd families.

sections.label: Scaling up KidSTART
sections.summary: Expresses concern about scaling the programme faster and welcomes KidSTART expansion, suggesting more corporate and community partner involvement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: My biggest concern with this programme is whether it can be scaled up faster.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I am therefore heartened to hear the recent announcement on the expansion of KidSTART and the launch of growing together with KidSTART at the Early Childhood conference last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Perhaps one way to scale the programme is to have more involvement from corporate and community partners who can help replicate the programme and support more families.

sections.label: Community partners lifting children
sections.summary: Community partners can play a special role in lifting up children, communities and Singaporeans, especially children starting with less.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, what these stories tell us, is that community partners can play a very special role in helping to lift up our children, in helping to lift up communities, in helping to lift up our fellow Singaporeans and especially children, who are starting with less.

sections.label: Social capital and KidSTART partnerships
sections.summary: The speaker asks MSF for updates on corporate and community partnerships, citing social capital research and KidSTART's expansion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: When we share social capital, it multiplies and it lifts up everyone even as we connect together, grow together, grow closer together as one Singapore family together, as Singapore together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: Whether you are looking at the research by Raj Chetty and his colleagues in the US, whether you listen to the stories by researchers such as Angus Deaton, all these researchers who have looked at inequality in society, who look at the role of neighbourhoods and how people's lives change over time – my belief is that a key question in all this, is the role of social capital and we must continue looking at it closely, developing it, growing it further.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to bring that social capital together in our society, it also helps to bring different stakeholders together to bring corporations and community partners together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: And as we heard recently at the Early Childhood conference in September last year, the Minister for MSF announced the expansion of KidSTART and growing together with KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: So, if I may ask the Minister, can MSF share any updates on the types of partnerships with corporates and community partners forged so far, because it takes all of us to make Singapore better and part of that journey to building a more fair and more equitable society is how we grow that social capital among us, how we grow the networks among us and how through that we uplift one another.

sections.label: Preschool subsidies and Partner Operator
sections.summary: Preschool subsidies were increased in January and the Partner Operator scheme will be extended for another five-year term from January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In January, we increased the preschool subsidies for low- and middle income families and enabled more families to benefit from the Additional Subsidy by raising the monthly household income ceiling from $7,500 to $12,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To enable more families to access affordable and quality preschool, we will extend the Partner Operator scheme for another five-year term, starting from January 2021.

sections.label: KidSTART expansion to more children
sections.summary: Following positive feedback, KidSTART will be expanded to reach 5,000 more children and their families over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: With the positive feedback, we will expand KidSTART to reach 5,000 more children and their families over the next three years.

sections.label: Student care subsidies for lower income
sections.summary: Subsidies will be increased to make student care more affordable and accessible for lower income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For some parents, student care services can fill this gap by providing a structured and conducive after-school environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will increase subsidies to make student care more affordable and accessible for lower income families.

sections.label: MSF amendments and capability building
sections.summary: MSF has worked with community partners and agencies on implementation and capability building, aiming to bring the first amendments into effect in the second quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: MSF has been working with community partners and agencies on implementation and capability building.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We aim to bring the first set of amendments into effect in the second quarter of this year.

sections.label: Triple P and Parenting Support Providers
sections.summary: Triple P is offered in 295 schools with over 20,000 parents attending, and 10 social service agencies were appointed as regional Parenting Support Providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 2014, we piloted Triple P in Primary and Secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Today, Triple P is offered in 295 Primary and Secondary schools in Singapore, and over 20,000 parents have attended.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Last year, we decided to put in more structure to our upstream family support and anchor upstream support at the regional and community level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And so, we appointed 10 social service agencies as regional Parenting Support Providers or PSPs.

sections.label: Online counselling pilot with Community Psychology Hub
sections.summary: MSF will run a two-year pilot with the Community Psychology Hub for online counselling via live chat or email later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Both this enhanced programme and the online portal will be ready in the later part of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To overcome this, MSF will implement a two-year pilot with the Community Psychology Hub to provide online counselling through live chat or email later this year.

sections.label: SG Enable as single touchpoint
sections.summary: SG Enable will be the single touchpoint for disability services, with related functions transferred from MSF headquarters and NCSS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To better support persons with disabilities and their care-givers, SG Enable will be the single touchpoint for disability services and public education efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Accordingly, disability service-related functions and programmes currently under MSF headquarters and the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) will be transferred to SG Enable.

sections.label: Special student care subsidies
sections.summary: Subsidies for special student care will increase across all income tiers and the income cap will be raised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To better support persons with disabilities and their care-givers, we will make special student care service much more affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will increase the subsidy quantum across all income tiers to reduce what parents have to pay out of pocket and raise the income cap so that more families can qualify.

sections.label: Community Link at four locations
sections.summary: MSF will launch Community Link, or ComLink, at Jalan Kukoh, Marsiling, Kembangan-Chai Chee and Boon Lay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: At last year's COS, I announced that MSF will be launching Community Link, or ComLink, at four locations – Jalan Kukoh, Marsiling, Kembangan-Chai Chee and Boon Lay.

sections.label: Local implementation workgroups engaging families
sections.summary: Local implementation workgroups went door-to-door to engage families with young children and held focus group discussions to understand their needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Over the past year, local implementation workgroups comprising social service agencies, schools and pre-schools, Government agencies, and the grassroots went door-to-door to engage all families with young children, and conducted focus group discussions to understand their needs, worries, strengths and aspirations.

sections.label: Home work café at Residents' Network
sections.summary: A local workgroup created a home work café at the Residents' Network, funded by South West CDC with NTU student tutors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To address this, the local implementation workgroup created a home work café at the Residents' Network, with South West CDC contributing funding and NTU students volunteering as tutors.

sections.label: Etonhouse donated Boxes of Joy
sections.summary: Etonhouse Community Fund donated over 800 Boxes of Joy with toys and educational materials to families in all four ComLink areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For instance, Etonhouse Community Fund donated more than 800 Boxes of Joy with brand-new toys and educational materials to families living in all four ComLink areas in December last year.

sections.label: Financial aid for quarantine orders
sections.summary: Financial assistance is provided for persons under Quarantine Orders or Stay-Home Notices in financial need, with The Courage Fund at $3.6 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, we provide financial assistance for persons under Quarantine Orders or Stay-Home Notices, if they are in financial need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We are also tapping on The Courage Fund which now stands at $3.6 million to provide additional support for lower income families who are affected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Share-the-Care baskets adopted
sections.summary: All 1,000 Share-the-Care baskets have been adopted, and families are hoped to continue paying the care forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: All 1,000 Share-the-Care baskets have been adopted and I hope families continue to pay the care forward.

sections.label: Youth Mental Well-being Network
sections.summary: Some are care-givers or therapists of persons with mental health issues, and a Youth Mental Well-being Network will be established.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Some are care-givers or therapists of persons with mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will be establishing a Youth Mental Well-being Network.

sections.label: Community Capability Trust fund
sections.summary: A Community Capability Trust of up to $480 million will be introduced, with $200 million initial capital and $2 matching per dollar donated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister during Budget, we will introduce the Community Capability Trust (CCT).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This is a dedicated, long-term fund of up to $480 million to strengthen our social service agencies capability and capacity to do more and to do so better.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Government and Tote Board will provide an initial $200 million in capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To encourage donors to contribute to capability building, the Government and Tote Board will match $2 to every dollar donated by the community for five years, from FY2020 to FY2024.

sections.label: Video conferencing at SSOs
sections.summary: Video conferencing at SSOs lets clients access agencies like HDB, WSG and Legal Aid Bureau without multiple trips, and the network will grow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Most of these services are provided at the SSOs through video conferencing to other agencies, making it more convenient for clients who need not make multiple trips to receive support from agencies such as HDB, Workforce Singapore (WSG) and the Legal Aid Bureau.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will grow this video conferencing network by offering access to more of these services at all our SSOs, and by bringing partners such as Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and hospitals into the network, over the next year.

sections.label: Enhanced system for frontline officers
sections.summary: Enhancements rolled out from the second half of this year will let about 5,000 frontline officers provide coordinated support and reduce the bandwidth tax on families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This will also reduce the bandwidth tax on families as they seek to tackle the challenges they face.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These enhancements will be rolled out from the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In steady state, about 5,000 frontline officers from both Government and community agencies will be able to tap on the enhanced system to provide comprehensive, convenient and coordinated support to the Singaporeans that we serve.

sections.label: SG Cares Community Network sessions
sections.summary: The first wave of 19 SG Cares Community Network sessions in 2019 brought together over 3,500 participants from 160 Government and community help agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The sessions spark discussions that turn into collaborative projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We completed the first wave of 19 SG Cares Community Network sessions island-wide in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Through these sessions, we brought together more than 3,500 participants from 160 Government and community help agencies.

sections.label: Youth mental well-being network
sections.summary: Noting higher prevalence of mental health conditions among those aged 18 to 34, a youth mental well-being network will be set up and views invited.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that young people between 18 and 34 years of age have a higher prevalence of mental health conditions as compared to older groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In total, more than 700 individuals and organisations have responded, many of whom are young people who are concerned about this issue and want to do something about it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will set up a youth mental well-being network and invite those who are passionate about this topic to share their views.

sections.label: Initiatives with Singaporeans
sections.summary: Initiatives include KidSTART, a marriage portal, ComLink, PEERS, the Community Capability Trust and the Youth Mental Well-being Network, with Singaporeans invited to join.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: I also spoke about several initiatives that we will work together with Singaporeans on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These include GROWING TOGETHER with KidSTART to support low income families with young children; an online portal for those facing difficulties in their marriage; ComLink to uplift families living in rental housing; the PEERS network to assist rough sleepers; the Community Capability Trust to build capability and capacity in the sector; and the Youth Mental Well-being Network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: I hope more Singaporeans will step forward to join us in these initiatives, participate in our Community Network sessions or join a Volunteer Centre set up by MCCY in their town.

sections.label: SG Enable single touchpoint
sections.summary: From 1 October 2020, SG Enable becomes the single touchpoint for the disability sector, taking over disability programmes run by MSF and NCSS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We are grateful to our partners and stakeholders, and have been making efforts to streamline service delivery for the disability sector based on their feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: So, I am pleased to announce that from 1 October 2020, SG Enable will become the single touchpoint for the disability sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: It will take over the administration of disability programmes currently run by MSF and the National Council of Social Service (NCSS).

sections.label: SG Enable leads disability public education
sections.summary: SG Enable will lead public education efforts related to disability to make public education messages stronger and clearer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: To make our public education messages stronger and clearer, SG Enable will lead public education efforts related to disability.

sections.label: Workgroups engagement sessions consultations
sections.summary: The workgroups held 13 engagement sessions and consulted more than 200 PWDs, care-givers and over 40 SSAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The workgroups have worked with Government and community partners over 13 engagement sessions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We consulted more than 200 PWDs, care-givers and over 40 different SSAs from the disability sector.

sections.label: Workgroups to submit recommendations
sections.summary: All three workgroups took in findings from the engagement sessions and will put up recommendations later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: All the three workgroups have taken in findings from the engagement sessions and will put up their recommendations later this year.

sections.label: MSF improves funding for SSCC families
sections.summary: MSF will improve funding and subsidy support for families of SSCC students and extend subsidies to more families of SPED students from 1 July 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: They are particularly essential for care-givers who need to work or care for other dependents and themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: I am therefore happy to announce that MSF will improve funding and subsidy support for families of SSCC students and extend the subsidies to more families of Special Education (SPED) students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: From 1 July 2020, we will raise the eligibility criteria for means-tested subsidies from $4,000 to $9,200, and we will also lower out-of-pocket expenses for SSCC services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: This reduces the out-of-pocket cost for a child from a family with a combined household income of $4,000 by around 75%, or from currently $582 to $142 a month, starting from July.

sections.label: SG Enable launches Enabling Guide website
sections.summary: SG Enable launched a new online website called "The Enabling Guide" in July last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: To this end, SG Enable launched a new online website called "The Enabling Guide" in July last year.

sections.label: MSF introduces ADAP deputyship programme
sections.summary: MSF introduced the Assisted Deputyship Application Programme to make the deputyship application process simpler and cheaper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: MSF has also introduced the Assisted Deputyship Application Programme (ADAP) to make the deputyship application process simpler and cheaper.

sections.label: Special Student Care Centre subsidies
sections.summary: From 1 July 2020, MSF will raise subsidy eligibility from $4,000 to $9,200 and lower SSCC out-of-pocket costs for SPED students' families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: From 1 July 2020, MSF will enhance subsidies to make Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs) services more affordable for families of Special Education (SPED) school students and will extend the subsidies to more families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We will raise the eligibility criteria for means-tested subsidies from $4,000 to $9,200, and lower out-of-pocket expenses for SSCC services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The reductions will range between 30% and 80% for most families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: This means that out-of-pocket cost for a child from a family with a combined household income of $4,000 will be reduced by around 75%, from $582 to $142 a month.

sections.label: Subsidies for low-income families
sections.summary: From August 2020, children in public rental flats or on ComCare assistance will automatically get maximum pre-school subsidies regardless of mother's working status.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To help low-income families further, we will streamline subsidy support under Special Approval for children living in public rental flats or receiving ComCare Short-to-Medium Term or ComCare Long-Term Assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From August 2020, these families will qualify for maximum pre-school subsidies automatically until the next fixed point of assessment, regardless of the mother’s working status.

sections.label: KidSTART expansion and income criterion
sections.summary: KidSTART will expand to 5,000 more children over three years, and its income criterion rises from $1,900 to $2,500 from April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have received positive feedback on the KidSTART pilot.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Thus, we are expanding KidSTART to another 5,000 children over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will also raise the KidSTART income eligibility criterion from a monthly household income of $1,900 to $2,500 from April this year, so that more families can benefit from it.

sections.label: Lower fee caps at pre-schools
sections.summary: Over the medium term, fee caps at Government-supported pre-schools will be lowered so working families pay around $300 monthly for full-day childcare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Over the medium-term, we aim to lower fee caps at Government-supported pre-schools so that working families with a child in full-day childcare will pay around $300 per month.

sections.label: Single Infrastructure Support Grant
sections.summary: ECDA will enhance funding amounts and streamline three schemes into a single Infrastructure Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Moving forward, ECDA will enhance the funding amounts and streamline the three schemes into a single Infrastructure Support Grant.

sections.label: Pre-schools close on Teachers' Day
sections.summary: From this year onward, all pre-schools will be required to close on Teachers' Day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We are also doing more to raise the standing of the profession.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we will make it mandatory for all pre-schools to close on Teachers’ Day from this year onward.

sections.label: DS-Plus programme for children
sections.summary: The DS-Plus programme lets children who progressed sufficiently under EIPIC receive intervention in the pre-school setting instead.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The new DS-Plus programme allows children who have made sufficient progress under EIPIC to receive intervention within the pre-school setting instead.

sections.label: Subsidies for low-income families
sections.summary: From August 2020, children from low-income families in public rental flats or on ComCare assistance automatically qualify for maximum pre-school subsidies under Special Approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Mr Seah Kian Peng also asked if we can do more for non-working mothers from low-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am glad to announce that with effect from August 2020, we will streamline subsidy support under Special Approval for all children from low-income families living in public rental flats, or receiving ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term or Long-Term Assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As these families have already been means-tested, we will automatically qualify them for maximum pre-school subsidies under Special Approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The subsidies will also remain unchanged until the next fixed point of assessment, as opposed to the current process where they may have to re-apply for support every few months.

sections.label: Lisa's monthly subsidy amount
sections.summary: With the enhanced subsidy process, Lisa will receive maximum subsidies and pay $3 per month until Caden completes Nursery 2.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: With our enhanced subsidy process, Lisa will receive maximum subsidies and continue to pay $3 per month until Caden completes Nursery 2.

sections.label: Pre-school Opportunity Fund extension
sections.summary: ECDA will extend the Pre-school Opportunity Fund for all other pre-schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For all other pre-schools, I am pleased to announce that ECDA will extend the Pre-school Opportunity Fund (PSOF).

sections.label: KidSTART expansion and income ceiling
sections.summary: KidSTART is expanding to another 5,000 children over three years, and from April the household income ceiling rises from $1,900 to $2,500.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Health and development issues were detected earlier, and younger children on KidSTART enrolled earlier in pre-school.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This is why we are expanding KidSTART to another 5,000 children over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From April onwards, we will also raise the household income ceiling from $1,900 to $2,500 to benefit more children.

sections.label: Student Care Fee Assistance enhancements
sections.summary: From 1 July 2020, SCFA subsidies increase by up to $60 monthly, income criteria rise to $4,500 and per capita income to $1,125, benefiting around 9,000 students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We want to ensure that student care remains affordable, especially for low-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am pleased to announce that we will increase the amount of subsidies under the Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA) scheme from 1 July 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Eligible families will receive up to $60 more subsidies each month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To benefit more families, we will also raise the income criteria from $4,000 to $4,500, and the per capita income from $1,000 to $1,125.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Around 9,000 students will benefit from these enhancements this year.

sections.label: MSF disability engagement sessions
sections.summary: MSF and partners held 13 engagement sessions with over 200 persons with disabilities, care-givers and social service agencies over almost four months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In the course of almost four months, MSF, together with partners and also the two co-chairman of the Enabling Masterplan 3 (EMP3) workgroups – Ms Denise Phua and Ms Chia Yong Yong – together we have engaged, we have conducted 13 engagement sessions with more than 200 persons with disabilities, the care-givers as well as the social service agencies from the disability sector.

sections.label: New independent living and employment initiatives
sections.summary: The engagement sessions identified 12 Independent Living initiatives and 14 Inclusive Employment initiatives, totalling 26 initiatives with 19 Government agencies and Ministries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Through these engagement sessions, we have currently identified 12 new initiatives under the workgroup for Independent Living as well as 14 initiatives for the workgroup for Inclusive Employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We now have 26 initiatives that we are working on together with 19 Government agencies and Ministries.

sections.label: Care-givers Pod for parents
sections.summary: SG Enable set up a dedicated Care-givers Pod as a meeting place for parents of children with disabilities or special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: To the question of what we do to help our care-givers, particularly parents with children with disabilities or special needs, SG Enable has set up a dedicated place called Care-givers Pod which serves as a meeting place for parents with special needs children or with disabilities to meet regularly.

sections.label: Donations for essentials and transport
sections.summary: Donations can be used for essentials like milk and diapers, transport costs for KidSTART and pre-school, and topping up CDA accounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The donations that we receive, we can use it for essentials such as milk, diapers as well as to help them with transport costs going for KidSTART programme as well as to pre-school.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: At the same time, there are also opportunities where we can help to top up their CDA account.

sections.label: Community Link in four locations
sections.summary: Community Link or ComLink was set up in four locations: Marsiling, Jalan Kukoh, Boon Lay and Kembangan-Chai Chee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Member is referring to Community Link or ComLink.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have set up Community Link in four locations for a start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the north, Marsiling; in the south, Jalan Kukoh; in the west, Boon Lay; and in the East, Kembangan-Chai Chee.
